title: Define tiered SLO config schema + loader w/ validation and safe rollout flags
author: Aisha Bello
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a canonical SLO configuration schema for Redwood’s tiered SLO program (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a runtime loader that validates configs, enforces guardrails, and supports a safe rollout path (dry-run + soft-fail + hard-fail modes). The schema is per tier/region/endpoint class, designed to keep metric cardinality controlled while still enabling multi-window burn-rate alerting and tier-aware dashboards.

Motivation / Context: We need a single source of truth for SLO definitions that can be consumed by: (1) SLO budget computation job, (2) recording rules + burn-rate alerts, (3) Console dashboards, and (4) deploy gate policy checks. Prior work has SLI queries evolving in multiple places and drift between Hosted and Dedicated. This PR implements the config substrate and validation so later PRs can rely on consistent naming and semantics.

Scope: In-scope SLOs in this schema: request success rate (non-5xx), end-to-end latency percentiles, streaming reliability (disconnect/error events). In-scope tiers: hosted, dedicated. Private is not modeled yet (explicitly rejected by validator).

Design highlights:
- Config format: YAML (checked into repo) with a JSON-schema definition (for editor tooling + CI validation).
- Primary keys: tier, region, endpoint_class, window (rolling), and objective.
- Endpoint classes: chat_completions, completions, embeddings, rerank, streaming_chat (streamed responses).
- Regions: enumerated set (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) to avoid exploding config fanout.
- Objectives supported:
  - availability: target (e.g., 99.9) and error_classification (what counts as bad)
  - latency: percentile (p95/p99) and threshold_ms
  - streaming: metric key for disconnect/error accounting (server-side only)
- Exclusions: encoded as allowlist of SLI filters (invalid_request, auth_error, rate_limited, customer_client_abort) so we don’t vary exclusions ad-hoc across tiers.
- Safe rollout flags:
  - loader.mode = off | dry_run | soft_fail | hard_fail
  - allow_partial = true/false (whether to load configs even when a subset fails validation)
  - required_coverage_min = 0.95 (guardrail for coverage validation; blocks hard-fail if we’re missing too much)
- Coverage validation: optional (enabled in CI by default, soft-fail in runtime) checks that the referenced metric names/labels exist in our telemetry catalog (via telemetry service API stub + cached manifest). This prevents shipping configs that can’t ever compute.

Implementation details:
- New package: internal/slo_config
  - Schema model structs + parsing
  - Validation passes:
    - schema validation (JSON schema)
    - semantic validation (tier/region/endpoint enums, duplicates, window sanity, objective ranges)
    - policy validation (Hosted/Dedicated constraints; e.g. dedicated must specify region explicitly; hosted can default to ‘global’ rollup entries but those are expanded deterministically)
    - metric reference validation (optional)
  - Loader:
    - loads from repo path config/slo/tiered/*.yaml
    - supports hot reload in control-plane (behind feature flag) but currently only wired into CLI + CI
- New CLI: tools/slo-config validate
  - validates all configs
  - prints normalized expanded config and validation summary
  - exit codes aligned with loader.mode
- CI integration:
  - adds a job slo-config-validate to required checks
  - ‘dry_run’ behavior in CI is disallowed; CI always uses hard-fail unless explicitly overridden in emergency (requires CODEOWNERS approval)

Files / areas changed (high level):
- config/slo/tiered/hosted.yaml (initial Hosted targets placeholders; will be updated in PM approval step)
- config/slo/tiered/dedicated.yaml (initial Dedicated targets placeholders; includes stricter latency defaults)
- internal/slo_config/* (schema, parser, validator, loader)
- tools/slo-config/* (CLI command)
- .github/workflows/ci.yaml (adds slo-config-validate step)
- docs/internal/sre/tiered-slo-config.md (dev notes + examples)

Example config snippet (illustrative):
- tier: dedicated
  region: eu-west-1
  endpoint_class: chat_completions
  window: 28d
  objectives:
    - type: availability
      target_percent: 99.9
      bad_events: ["5xx", "gateway_timeout", "stream_server_disconnect"]
      exclusions: ["invalid_request", "auth_error", "rate_limited", "client_abort"]
    - type: latency
      percentile: p95
      threshold_ms: 900

Notes / Non-goals:
- This PR does not create Prometheus recording rules or burn-rate alert definitions. It provides the typed/validated inputs those PRs will use.
- This PR does not wire deploy gates to the new config yet.
- This PR does not define final SLO targets; current values are marked as provisional and will be updated once PM-812 is approved.

Testing:
- Unit tests for parsing/validation (good configs, duplicate keys, invalid windows, out-of-range targets, disallowed tiers)
- Golden tests for normalization/expansion (hosted global entries expand into per-region set)
- CI added: slo-config-validate

Rollout plan:
1) Land schema + loader (this PR)
2) Switch alerting PR to consume normalized config (PR-28492)
3) Switch budget computation job to consume normalized config (ENG-4934)
4) Switch deploy gate policy checks to reference budget state keyed by (tier, region, endpoint_class)

Review notes requested:
- Please focus on semantic validation constraints and the expansion logic (hosted global -> per-region).
- Confirm that metric reference validation approach won’t cause fragile CI failures due to telemetry catalog lag.

Linked: ENG-4926 (build SLO config schema and validation), ENG-4921 (define tiered SLIs and exclusions)

---
Commits:
1) slo_config: add schema model + YAML parsing
2) slo_config: semantic validator + normalization/expansion
3) tools: add slo-config validate CLI
4) ci: add slo-config-validate required check
5) config: add initial hosted/dedicated tiered SLO config skeletons

---
Review conversation (abridged):
- Allison Grant: Can we lock down label enums to prevent future drift (e.g., endpoint_class names)? Also please document where latency is measured (gateway vs serving).
  - Aisha Bello: Added enums + explicit endpoint_class list; updated docs to state latency SLI is measured at API gateway e2e for this program.
- Thomas Baird: Concern on hosted ‘global’ expansion creating silent duplicates when region list changes. Need deterministic expansion + test.
  - Aisha Bello: Implemented deterministic expansion from a single region enum source; added golden test asserting expanded keys.
- Logan Wright: Metric reference validation calling telemetry service could be flaky in CI; can we use a cached manifest with pinned version?
  - Aisha Bello: Updated to use repo-pinned manifest by default; live catalog only in manual mode; CI uses pinned manifest.
- Jordan Lee: We need loader.mode to be controllable for future deploy-gate integration; suggest off/dry_run/soft_fail/hard_fail and log structured events.
  - Aisha Bello: Added loader.mode and structured log events (slo_config_validation_failed with reason codes).

Approvals:
- Allison Grant: Approved
- Thomas Baird: Approved
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Jordan Lee: Approved

CI:
- build-and-test: pass
- lint: pass
- slo-config-validate: pass

Merge: Squash merged into main on 2026-02-07.
